body.text: The covered launchpad fee subtotal for 2026-W42 (Oct 12, 2026 to Oct 18, 2026, UTC) was $23.96M across 14 non-overlapping venues, −21.0% against 2026-W41 on the same venues. 5 venues that share a fee stream with another venue are reported individually and never added.
Creator earnings — fees paid to coin creators and, depending on the venue's own definition, holders, referrers or traders — were $12.25M across 15 venues that define them, −24.8% week over week.
By share of the subtotal, pump.fun gained the most (+3.6 points) and LaunchLab lost the most (-1.6 points). A share shift says where fees moved, not why.

Trading in the coins of the tracked narratives totalled $397.88M for the week, counting a coin once when it belongs to more than one narrative (the per-narrative totals add up to $413.61M). This is the volume of identified coins across their indexed pools, not of the whole market.

Perpetual-futures coins carried the most volume among narratives collected during the week: $128.07M (partial: some member-days were not observed). It was first observed this week, so no week-over-week change is reported.

First observed this week: Perpetual-futures coins, Flying Tesla Roadster coins, Coins paired with tokenized stocks, Creator fees routed to people, AI credits for holders. A narrative's first week has no meaningful prior week, so no change is reported for it.

Collection paused during the week: AI credits for holders, Launchpad coins with on-chain rules, Tokenized stocks and RWA coins, Agency living tokens, Post-quantum coins. Their members stay members; their totals after the pause are partial, not zero.
